findings.title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: In UsernameForm.authenticate() the new condition calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The only method with that name is the one this PR adds to the superclass UsernamePasswordForm, declared as isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). UsernameForm declares no zero-argument overload, and none exists in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, so this line cannot compile and the services module build fails. It presumably should be isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, so passkeys UI disappears on all fresh logins
findings.body: The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, and both call sites pass context.getUser() (authenticate() at line 115 and challenge(context, error, field) at line 137). On a normal, non-reauthentication login context.getUser() is null, so the condition is false and webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked for fresh logins. Previously the form was filled exactly in that case ("user is not already selected"). As a result the username/password page is rendered without the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes (enableWebAuthnConditionalUI, challenge, rpId) for anonymous users, completely breaking passkey autofill / discoverable-key login on first-time logins — the primary scenario the passkeys feature exists for — including after a failed first login attempt (the error challenge also loses the WebAuthn markup). The PR's own tests would fail, e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey expects automatic login from a fresh login form and several tests assert //form[@id='webauth'] is present on fresh login pages. The user check should be inverted or dropped (e.g. allow a null user, and for the re-authentication case optionally verify the identified user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential).
